observation_summary: The compiler's peephole optimization incorrectly folded array access expressions by ignoring side effects in array elements that were discarded during the folding process, leading to incorrect code transformation.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves modifying the loop logic in 'tryFoldArrayAccess' to iterate through all array elements and check for side effects using 'mayHaveSideEffects' before deciding whether to fold the expression. This is a procedural change to the optimization algorithm, ensuring that side effects are preserved, rather than a simple guard or initialization error.
evidence_used: The fix diff adds a loop-based check for side effects on elements that are not the target of the array access.
The bug report states: 'tryFoldArrayAccess in com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeFoldConstants should check whether every array element that is not going to be preserved has no side effects.'
The fix modifies the loop structure to iterate through all elements and perform a conditional check.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds a check, the check is part of a broader algorithmic requirement to validate the safety of an optimization transformation, not just a simple parameter or boundary guard.
